name: justlogic_bronze
description: JustLogicBronze is a compact 22-question deductive logic benchmark adapted from the JustLogic dataset, restricted to depth-1 reasoning. Each item presents natural-language premises and asks whether a claim is TRUE, FALSE, or Uncertain given only those premises. It covers core inference rules (Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens, Disjunctive Syllogism, Disjunction Elimination, Reductio Ad Absurdum) with heavy surface-form variation, including distractor claims that differ subtly from the entailed conclusion. Intended as an entry-level suite; scores should not be compared with deeper-reasoning logic benchmarks.

questions.question: ALWAYS USE WORLD MODELS TO ANSWER THE QUESTION: Premises: One may reasonably assume that if the statement that 'democracy helps people to protect their own fundamental interests' is incorrect, then pluralisms are doctrines. Provided that the statement that 'democracy helps people to protect their own fundamental interests' is incorrect, we know that some people mistakenly believe that pluralisms are doctrines. Based only on the premises, is the following claim TRUE, FALSE, or Uncertain? Claim: Those that suggest democracy helps people to protect their own fundamental interests are right.
questions.notes: Reductio: If (Not [0]), then [1]; If (Not [0]), then (Not [1]); therefore [0]. Statements: 0=Democracy helps people protect their own fundamental interests; 1=Pluralisms are doctrines.

questions.question: ALWAYS USE WORLD MODELS TO ANSWER THE QUESTION: Premises: At least one of two things is true: either basic competency is defined as reading, writing, mathematics, and science or excess prostaglandins make the smooth muscles contract, or either international health means two different, but related, things or statistics show that there are more women in the world than anything else - except insects. The claim that either basic competency is defined as reading, writing, mathematics, and science or excess prostaglandins make the smooth muscles contract has no merit. Based only on the premises, is the following claim TRUE, FALSE, or Uncertain? Claim: It is a fact that either international health means two different, but related, things or statistics come in many forms and interpretations.
questions.notes: Disjunctive Syllogism yields 'Either [0] or [1]' but the claim swaps statement 1 for a different statement ('statistics come in many forms'). Statements: 0=International health means two different, but related, things; 1=Statistics show there are more women than anything else except insects; 2=Basic competency definition; 3=Excess prostaglandins make smooth muscles contract.
